SHREEJI INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED
Plot 66, GIDC Makarpura, Vadodara 390010, Gujarat

STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
SOP NO. PUR-SOP-004: SUPPLIER ONBOARDING, EVALUATION AND PAYMENT

Revision: 2
Effective Date: 1 June 2026
Prepared by: Purchase Manager (Mr. Hitesh Vyas)
Reviewed by: Finance Controller (Ms. Pooja Trivedi)
Approved by: Managing Director
Next Review: 31 May 2027

1. OBJECTIVE

1.1 To lay down a uniform procedure for selecting, verifying, approving, onboarding and paying suppliers (vendors) of goods and services, so that the Company buys the right quality at the right price, from compliant suppliers, with proper approvals and statutory compliance.

2. SCOPE

2.1 This SOP applies to every supplier of raw materials, components, packaging, consumables, capital goods and services, whether new or existing, and to all departments raising purchase requisitions.

2.2 One-time purchases of less than Rs 10,000 through petty cash are exempt from Steps 3 to 7 but must still be recorded in the petty cash register.

3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "Vendor Master" means the supplier database maintained in the ERP system by the Purchase Department and the Finance Department.

3.2 "Class A Vendor" means a supplier of critical materials or services, where a failure would stop production within seven (7) days, or whose annual business with the Company is expected to exceed Rs 50 lakh.

3.3 "Class B Vendor" means a supplier of regular materials and services with annual business between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 50 lakh.

3.4 "Class C Vendor" means a supplier of non-critical items, consumables and occasional services, with annual business below Rs 10 lakh.

3.5 "MSME Vendor" means a supplier that holds a valid Udyam Registration under the MSMED Act, 2006, in the category of micro or small enterprise.

4. PROCEDURE

Step 1 - Identification and requisition. The user department identifies the need and raises a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the ERP, with specifications, quantity, required date and budget code. A PR for a new supplier shall be accompanied by the name of the proposed supplier and the reason for selecting the supplier.

Step 2 - Sourcing and quotations. The Purchase Department shall obtain at least three (3) written quotations for every purchase of Rs 1,00,000 and above, and at least two (2) quotations for purchases between Rs 25,000 and Rs 99,999. Single-source purchases require a written justification approved by the Purchase Manager.

Step 3 - Supplier registration form. The proposed new supplier shall fill the Supplier Registration Form (Form PUR-F-01) in full, giving details of the constitution, directors or partners, products, capacity, key customers, bank account, and contact persons, and shall sign the Supplier Code of Conduct.

Step 4 - Submission of documents. The supplier must submit the documents listed in Clause 5 below. A supplier that does not submit all the required documents shall not be entered in the Vendor Master.

Step 5 - Verification and due diligence. The Purchase Department, with the Finance Department, shall verify the documents as follows:
(a) Verify the PAN on the Income Tax e-filing portal, and verify that the PAN is operative and linked with Aadhaar, where the supplier is an individual or proprietor.
(b) Verify the GSTIN on the GST common portal and check the status ("Active"), the legal name, the constitution of business and the filing frequency, and also check the last six months of Form GSTR-3B filing status. A supplier whose GSTIN is cancelled or suspended, or who has not filed returns for two (2) or more consecutive months, shall not be onboarded.
(c) Verify the Udyam Registration Number on the Udyam portal, for MSME Vendors.
(d) Verify the bank account by a penny-drop test of Re 1, and check the name of the account holder against the name in the GST registration.
(e) Search the supplier and its directors on the list of debarred or blacklisted entities, and the MCA21 portal for the status of the company (active or struck off), where the supplier is a company.
(f) For Class A Vendors, conduct a site visit or a quality system audit by Quality Assurance and Purchase, and prepare an audit report in Form PUR-F-04.

Step 6 - Evaluation and classification. The Purchase Manager shall score the supplier on quality, price, delivery capacity, financial stability, and compliance, on a scale of 100. A supplier must score at least 70 to be approved. A score of 85 or more shall be eligible for Class A.

Step 7 - Approval. The approval of the new supplier and of each purchase order shall be given in accordance with the approval matrix in Clause 6.

Step 8 - Creation in Vendor Master. After approval, the Finance Department shall create the supplier in the Vendor Master with a unique vendor code, the payment terms and the TDS section. The creation, and any later change in bank details, requires the approval of two persons: one from Purchase and one from Finance. A change of bank details can be made only on a written request on the letterhead of the supplier and after a call-back verification to a known contact person.

Step 9 - Purchase order. The purchase order shall be issued only from the ERP, in the name of the approved supplier, and shall state the item, quantity, price, GST rate, delivery date, payment terms and the quality requirements. Work shall not be started and goods shall not be received without a purchase order.

Step 10 - Receipt, inspection and invoice matching. Goods shall be received at the stores against the purchase order, and shall be inspected by Quality Assurance. The Goods Receipt Note (GRN) shall be made within one (1) working day. The supplier's invoice shall be matched in three ways: purchase order, GRN and invoice. Payment shall not be made if there is a mismatch of price or quantity.

Step 11 - Payment. Payment shall be made as per Clause 7, after verification of the invoice and the ITC position in GSTR-2B.

Step 12 - Periodic review. Every supplier shall be reviewed once a year, in April, on the basis of delivery performance, rejection rate and compliance. A supplier whose rejection rate exceeds 3% of the supplied quantity for two (2) successive quarters shall be placed on probation for six months. Suppliers who do not transact for 24 months shall be deactivated.

5. DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FROM THE SUPPLIER

5.1 PAN card of the supplier (company, firm, proprietor).
5.2 GST registration certificate (Form GST REG-06), and the GSTIN stated on invoices.
5.3 Udyam Registration Certificate (for MSME Vendors), failing which the supplier shall be treated as a non-MSME vendor.
5.4 Cancelled cheque or bank certificate, giving the account number, IFSC code and name of the account holder.
5.5 Certificate of incorporation, partnership deed or proprietorship declaration, as applicable, with the list of directors or partners and the authorised signatory.
5.6 Copy of MSME declaration in the Company's format, and a self-declaration that the supplier is not a related party, or a disclosure of the relationship.
5.7 Quality certificates, such as ISO 9001:2015, test reports, or material certificates, for Class A and Class B vendors.
5.8 Two (2) trade references, with contact details, for new Class A and B vendors.
5.9 Signed Supplier Code of Conduct, which covers anti-bribery, labour law compliance, child labour prohibition and safety.
5.10 Last two (2) years' financial statements, for Class A vendors, and for any supplier whose expected annual business exceeds Rs 25 lakh.

6. APPROVAL MATRIX (PURCHASE ORDERS AND NEW SUPPLIERS)

Order value (per purchase order, excluding GST)    | Approver
Up to Rs 50,000                                    | Department Head
Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000                           | Purchase Manager and Finance Controller
Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 25,00,000                        | General Manager - Operations
Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000                     | Managing Director / Director
Above Rs 1,00,00,000                               | Board of Directors
New supplier (any value)                           | Purchase Manager and Finance Controller, plus the approval above for the first PO
Single-source purchases above Rs 5,00,000          | General Manager - Operations in addition to the above

6.1 A purchase order may not be split to bring it within a lower approval limit. Splitting is a violation of this SOP.

6.2 Capital expenditure is governed by the Capital Expenditure Policy, which prevails over this clause.

7. PAYMENT TERMS

7.1 The standard payment terms, counted from the date of receipt of the goods or the acceptance of the services (whichever is later), or the date of receipt of a valid invoice, whichever is later, are as follows:

Vendor class                               | Payment term                  | Early-payment discount
Class A Vendor                             | 60 days                       | As negotiated, typically 1% if paid within 15 days
Class B Vendor                             | 45 days                       | 0.5% if paid within 10 days
Class C Vendor                             | 30 days                       | None
MSME Vendor (any class)                    | 30 days (never more than 45)  | Not applicable
Service providers and contractors          | 30 days from invoice          | None
Imports (letter of credit or advance)      | As per the LC / contract      | Not applicable

7.2 In accordance with Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006, payment to an MSME Vendor shall be made within the period agreed in writing, which shall in no case exceed forty-five (45) days from the day of acceptance. Where there is no written agreement, payment shall be made within fifteen (15) days of acceptance. Interest on delayed payment is payable at three times the bank rate with monthly rests, as provided in Section 16. The Finance Department shall run an ageing report every Monday for MSME Vendor invoices pending for more than 30 days.

7.3 Advance payments shall not exceed twenty per cent (20%) of the order value, and may be made only against a bank guarantee where the advance exceeds Rs 5,00,000. Advances to MSME Vendors may be released up to thirty per cent (30%) for tooling and special material.

7.4 Payment runs shall be made on every Tuesday and Friday, and only by NEFT, RTGS or UPI business payment, to the verified bank account. Cash payments are not permitted, except for petty cash up to Rs 5,000 a day.

7.5 Tax deduction at source shall be made at the applicable rates, including 1% for individuals and HUFs and 2% for other persons under Section 194C, 2% under Section 194J for technical services and 10% for professional services, and 0.1% under Section 194Q for the purchase of goods where the purchases from a supplier exceed Rs 50 lakh in a financial year. No payment shall be made to a supplier whose PAN is not furnished, and in such case TDS shall be deducted at 20%.

7.6 Payment under the reverse charge mechanism shall be made by the Company directly to the Government, and the ITC shall be taken in the month of payment.

8. COMPLIANCE AND RECORDS

8.1 The Finance Department shall verify on the 10th of every month that the ITC of the previous month, as reflected in GSTR-2B, matches the ITC to be claimed in GSTR-3B, and shall hold the payment of the GST portion for invoices of suppliers who have not filed GSTR-1.

8.2 All onboarding records shall be preserved for eight (8) years after the end of the financial year in which the relationship with the supplier ends.

8.3 A supplier who submits false documents, or offers any gift or inducement to any employee, shall be removed from the Vendor Master and blacklisted for a minimum period of three (3) years.

9. CONTACTS AND ESCALATION

9.1 Queries on supplier registration shall be addressed to the Purchase Department (purchase@shreeji-industrial.example). Payment queries shall be addressed to Accounts Payable (ap@shreeji-industrial.example). Disputes on payment shall be escalated to the Finance Controller within seven (7) days.

ANNEXURE - CHECKLIST FOR NEW SUPPLIER

[ ] Udyam verified               [ ] Cancelled cheque        [ ] Penny-drop done
[ ] Code of Conduct signed       [ ] Quality certificates    [ ] Approval as per Clause 6
